run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: I could not tie request REQ-EU-8K4M2 to any service from the available evidence. Two of the three telemetry sources that could attribute a single request — Jaeger (traces) and Prometheus (metrics/alerts) — were unreachable throughout this Run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on repeated attempts), so there are no spans, no error-rate series and no latency series for the window. What I could read does not localise the fault: the Elasticsearch geo logs hold 1620 indices app-185-geo-<region>-<service>-<date> for six regions including geo-eu-central and geo-eu-west and 27 services per EU region, but every document inside the authorized window in eu-central and eu-west is a level=INFO "Request completed successfully" heartbeat with response_time_ms=150 at 2026-11-22T09:12:00Z, and the index mapping has no request-id field, so the request ID cannot be resolved from logs (searches for the ID returned no documents). In the cluster, the 25 Deployments each report 1 ready/1 available replica, otel-demo fault-injection flags are all off in the flagd ConfigMap, and checkout's own logs show completed orders (payment went through, confirmation email sent) up to 09:12:45. The one genuine error stream I found is in otel-collector: repeated "failed to upload metrics … http2: frame too large … looked like an HTTP/1.1 header" failures every ~10 s from 09:11:47 to 09:13:57 against otel-collector:4318 — a telemetry-pipeline fault that plausibly explains missing metric data but is not shown to slow user requests. The only non-platform workload seen (Deployment blue-whale in namespace app-94) disappeared during the investigation while namespace app-94 went Terminating and a new namespace app-95 with Deployment orca appeared at 09:15:55, which looks like lab churn rather than the reported incident. No service can be named as affected on its own evidence, so no root cause is asserted.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch target holds 1620 indices following app-185-geo-<region>-<service>-<date> across six region groups: geo-ap-northeast, geo-ap-south, geo-eu-central, geo-eu-west, geo-us-east and geo-us-west, with 27 services per EU region (analytics, api, auth, billing, cache, cart, catalog, checkout, db, inventory, notification, orders, payments, pricing, profiles, promotions, ratings, recommendations, reviews, search, shipping, subscriptions, tracking, users, web, wishlist, worker).

The application-log mapping in the EU indices contains only @timestamp, level, message, region, response_time_ms and service — there is no request-id or trace-id field to look the customer's ID up by.

Inside the authorized window the eu-central indices hold 27 documents, one per service, all with @timestamp 2026-11-22T09:12:00Z, level INFO, message "Request completed successfully" and response_time_ms 150 (e.g. app-185-geo-eu-central-checkout-2024.01.10); the eu-west indices likewise match 27 documents, and the ones shown (analytics, api, auth, billing, cache) have the same INFO/150 ms values at the same timestamp.

The otel-collector container in otel-demo logged a repeating export failure every ~10 seconds between 2026-11-22T09:11:47Z and 09:13:57Z: "failed to upload metrics: reader collect and export timeout: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = \"error reading server preface: http2: failed reading the frame payload: http2: frame too large, note that the frame header looked like an HTTP/1.1 header\"", with a grpc transport error to Addr "10.96.247.55:4318", ServerName "otel-collector:4318".

The checkout container's logs between 2026-11-22T08:55:01Z and 09:12:45Z show completed order flows, e.g. "[PlaceOrder] user_id=… user_currency=USD", "payment went through (transaction_id: …)" and "order confirmation email sent to …" — i.e. checkout→payment→email completed for these requests before the response time.

The alerting configuration loaded into Prometheus contains one lab alert, CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh, on the ratio of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} > 0.5 over 5m for 2m (severity critical); the ConfigMap's separate "alerts" file content is "{}".

All otel-demo fault-injection flags read from the flagd ConfigMap (demo.flagd.json) are disabled: productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad each have state ENABLED but defaultVariant "off", and flagd is started with --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json mounted from that ConfigMap. No fault-enabling variable appears in the otel-demo Deployment env lists (which only carry ports, *_ADDR, FLAGD_HOST/PORT and OTLP settings).

All 25 Deployments in the cluster report 1 ready and 1 available replica (including every otel-demo service: ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart), and the only events inside the authorized window are six for the app-94 objects Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 (ScalingReplicaSet, SuccessfulCreate, Created, Scheduled, Pulled, Started) timestamped 2026-11-22T09:11:50Z.

The only non-platform workload observed was Deployment blue-whale in namespace app-94 (image python:3.9-slim, env DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20), and the Service postgres in app-94 (port 5432, selector app=postgres-db) had no endpoints subsets; the namespace app-94 was in phase Terminating at 09:15:47Z and no pod remained in it, while namespace app-95 was created at 09:15:55Z with a new Deployment orca (python:3.9-slim, SERVICE_NAME=orca-image-processor) created at 09:15:56Z.

Every otel-demo pod reports restartCount 2 (kube-state-metrics 4, prometheus-readonly-proxy 6) with the current containers started between 2026-11-22T08:04:19Z and 08:05:10Z, i.e. a cluster-wide restart roughly an hour before the response time.

The repeated otel-collector metric-upload failure (OTLP export to otel-collector:4318 answered by an HTTP/1.1-style server, "http2: frame too large") is a telemetry-pipeline fault that may explain why span-derived metric series and alert evaluation are unavailable for this window; it is not evidence that user request latency increased.

Deployment blue-whale in app-94 points its DB at postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local while that Service had no endpoints, so that app could have suffered DB connect failures or up-to-30-second connection timeouts (slow responses with an error page); nothing in the evidence links blue-whale to Europe or to REQ-EU-8K4M2, and it produced no log lines, so this remains unverified and is most likely lab scaffolding that was being torn down.

Rejected: that the European application logs themselves record the customer's failing request. The only EU documents in the window are uniform level=INFO, response_time_ms=150 successes at 2026-11-22T09:12:00Z (27 in eu-central, 27 in eu-west), and the mapping carries no request-id field at all.

Rejected as far as the declared configuration goes: that a fault-injection feature flag was switched on in otel-demo during the window. The flagd ConfigMap in effect lists every fault flag (cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, imageSlowLoad, etc.) with defaultVariant "off", and flagd loads exactly that file; a runtime override through flagd's in-memory store cannot be excluded from the ConfigMap alone.

Retry the trace lookup once Jaeger is reachable: search spans for the frontend/frontend-proxy/checkout services in the window with a request-id tag equal to REQ-EU-8K4M2, then fetch the whole trace by trace ID to see which server span first carries an error and which child client call (cart, payment, product-catalog, shipping, currency, email, recommendation, quote) is the long or failed one.

Once Prometheus answers, evaluate traces_span_metrics_calls_total by service_name/span_name/status_code (especially .*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count / http_server_request_duration_seconds_count over the window, and compare against a pre-window baseline before calling any latency trend real.

Check the otel-collector configuration (ConfigMap otel-collector, key relay) for an exporter pointed at otel-collector:4318 when the endpoint only speaks gRPC/HTTP2, since the logged "frame too large … looked like an HTTP/1.1 header" errors mean span metrics are not being uploaded and latency/error monitoring is blind.

gaps: Jaeger was unreachable for every attempt (traces_list_services, and traces_search for frontend and checkout, all SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span or trace exists for REQ-EU-8K4M2 and the request cannot be mapped to a service, operation or trace ID.

Prometheus was unreachable for every attempt (get_all_labels, get_metric_names, list_prometheus_rules, metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, all SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and app_payment_transactions_total could not be read; no error rate, no latency value and no firing-alert state (including CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh) is known for the window, and no latency trend can be stated without a baseline.

Searches of app-* and app-185-geo-eu-* for "REQ-EU-8K4M2", "REQ-EU", "8K4M2", "error", "timeout" and "slow" returned zero documents (no_data views); the log mapping has no request-id field, so whether the ID is logged at all is unknown, not disproven.

The frontend pod otel-demo/frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw returned 0 log lines (0 bytes read) for the window, so no HTTP status, URI or error page for the customer's request could be examined at the frontend.

The blue-whale pod in app-94 returned 0 log lines while it still existed and the namespace was then deleted (app-94 Terminating, pod gone at 09:15:47Z), so that workload's runtime errors and timings are unverifiable; whether blue-whale or its successor orca serves the European region is also undocumented.

The cause of the cluster-wide restart of all otel-demo pods (current containers started 08:04–08:05Z, restartCount 2–6) is not observed; no Evicted, OOMKilled or BackOff evidence was seen, and change history is not integrated (change_history not integrated in this Run).
Secret blue-whale-app (mounted as /app in the blue-whale Deployment) cannot be read, so the application code that would define its request IDs, error page and slow paths could not be verified.
kubernetes networkpolicies, ingresses, resourcequotas, jobs and persistentvolumeclaims queries returned no objects, so misconfiguration of those kinds cannot be confirmed or ruled out from this Run.
next_steps: Confirm with the customer the exact URL, timestamp and region of the error page behind REQ-EU-8K4M2, and whether the ID is rendered from an application log field or a frontend-generated identifier.
Re-run the Jaeger search (service frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout) restricted to 08:50–09:14Z with a request-id tag filter for REQ-EU-8K4M2 and pull the full trace by ID.

Re-run the Prometheus queries for per-service span error ratio and p95 latency in the window against a same-length baseline before the window, and check the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh alert state for the window.
Review and correct the otel-collector exporter configuration (OTLP HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP2 mismatch at otel-collector:4318) so span metrics and therefore latency/error dashboards and alerts resume.

content.alerting_rules:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
